notes.title: Another update for Food Truck Simulator is here! 🍣🔥
notes.content:

We’re back with a fresh update which will introduce some features that have been heavily requested by most of our players. Your support means a lot to us and pushes us forward on the development journey, so HUGE THANKS TO YOU, FOLKS!❤️‍🔥 Having said that, if you still encounter any issues with the game, make sure to let us know whether in the comment section below, Steam forums, or on our discord server. [*]Fixed Journal texts being all in caps – [i]It ain't much but it's honest work, ey[/i]

[*]Changed Sushi Recipes to require 3 pieces of fish instead of 5, meaning that you should no longer need to play Sushi Minigame multiple times to succeed, instead if played well you will get extra resources towards the next sushi – A[i]nd that's what we call a quality-of-life update! notes.title: Update #3 is here!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/55d7aaf08c885ea9ead8f9644c010ad8b14b12a1.jpg[/img]

Another update following the recently released Update #2 to address some issues that have been reported. We also made some more performance improvements while at it.

[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixes a crash issue with the upgraded cutting board and while at it we fixed the sushi problem, too.
[*] Fixes a potential crash during the competition.
[*] Fixes a problem with the Find Lucian’s Shop quest.
[*] Fixes an issue that caused map markers not showing after loading a game. 
[*] Fixes a bug that caused custom map markers to not always save correctly.
[*] Fixes a bug that caused the UI text to shake on the screen while fueling.
[*] Fixes multiple issues with lock picking. The way lock picking works under the hood has been 
[*] reworked in order to eliminate the issues reported.
[*] Fixes an issue that could cause inputs to be processed incorrectly when in the journal causing in turn the character to walk unintentionally.
[*] Fixes a bug that prevented the radio stations not to play.
[*] Fixes an issue with menu creator when aborting prematurely or switch tabs in the PC.
[*] Fixes an issue that prevented the Hurricane shop marker to be displayed correctly on the map.
[*] Fixes an issue with missing gas station thumbnail on the map. 
[*] Fixes a bug that caused fast travel icons to not unlock properly on the map.
[*] Added missing sounds when putting a pizza together.
[*] Fixes a bug when fuelling the truck that allowed to fuel it despite the tank already being full.
[*] Fixes a problem of not being able to interact correctly with Hurricane when ordering from Clara.
[*] Fixes a bug that made the mouse cursor disappear when in the shop tab.
[*] Fixes a bug that blocked UI buttons during sabotage and slashing tires.
[*] Fixes a bug that caused the confirmation popup on Save and Load to not close correctly.
[*] Fixes the problem with disappearing icons while driving.
[*] Fixes a bug that caused the achievements Serious Player and Local Hero to not register correctly.
[*] Fixes an issue with Clara’s job marker to being displayed correctly.
[/list]
[h3]Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] The Back to Shop button is now active during the quests with Luciano and Hurricane.
[*] Highlighting items has seen some improvement and should now be more responsive and better visible.
[*] The state of the jerrycan in the garage is now being properly saved.
[*] Saving and loading the state of jobs has been improved and should be a lot more reliable now.
[*] More tutorials in Free Roam have been added.
[*] The Journal tab has proper animations now. While at it, multiple photos in the journal have been fixed.
[*] Inventory items and now better displayed.
[*] Clara’s shop working hours in Free Roam have been adjusted.
[*] Vehicle AI has seen a series of smaller improvements.
[/list]
[h3]Performance[/h3]
[list]
[*] Various static meshes/objects in the game world has been further optimized for better performance.
[*] Reduced the amount of graphical assets being kept in memory even when not needed at any given time resulting in a smaller memory (RAM) footprint.
[/list]
[h3]Other[/h3]
[list]
[*] Spoken dialogs during sabotage has been shortened slightly.
[*] We hope we made the instructions for the map zoom feature a little bit clearer now.
[*] The tutorial for hacking should be a bit easier to understand now.
[*] Various language and translations updates.
[/list]

And that's it for today! We hope that you'll enjoy the update and the changes that we've made. If you still have any concerns about the game-related stuff, feel free to let us know in the comments below. Last but not least, we've just wanted to let you know that Food Truck Simulator along with Gas Station Simulator is currently on sale, so if you've ever dreamed of running a successful food truck or gas station business, now is the great chance to make a dream comes true!

notes.title: Update #2 is here!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/36e8def916a5206d4f58e598556f7f1a9b0a6302.jpg[/img]

Hey, chefs! 👋

It’s been a while since our last hotfix, so we thought that it was a good time to share some more information about what we’re working on. The team has been busy as popcorn on a skillet in order to bring you even more content to the game and fix major issues that players have encountered during their Food Truck journey🍔🚌 
We’ve gathered a lot of feedback from you, and based on that, we’ve added some improvements to the game.

Having said that, we’d really like to thank you for all for the support that we’ve received from you so far. Please, remember that if you run into any issues during the gameplay, feel free to drop us the message in the comment section below. As for this patch, it's larger than the previous one, so grab your favorite drink, relax, and enjoy the reading.⬇️


[h3]Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] A Menu Creator has been added to the game allowing you to create a menu out of existing recipes to be drawn from at selling points.
[*] You can now buy pre-cutted ingredients. These cost a bit more, but that’s the price you have to pay for gaining time.
[*] Improvements to handling randomization when drawing orders to prevent the same orders to appear subsequently too often.
[*] Improvements have been made to the map allowing you to zoom in/out and add custom markers to the map. The default setting for zooming is on the mouse wheel and brackets [ and ].
[/list]

[h3]Balancing[/h3]
[list]
[*] Requirements for devices/appliances have been rebalanced as some could be upgraded too early and other too late.
[*] Sushi container now only accepts rolls as we initially intended. The last update introduced a bug allowing placement of others things that lead to multiple bugs and issues down the road.
[*] Pizza dough freshness does not degrade that fast anymore.
[/list]

[h3]Performance[/h3]
[list]
[*] A series of performance improvements across the board in all areas of the game. This should result in smoother performance on most system and a significant reduction in stuttering.
[*] Many LODs in the game have been improved or reworked to improve visuals and increase performance.
[/list]

[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixes a bug that caused lock-up in the shop and thus preventing the Hurricane related quest to be completed correctly.  
[*] Fixes the issue that causes some markers on the map to displayed twice.
[*] Fixes a bug that caused the distance on markers to not be shown after loading a game.
[*] Fixes various issues, bugs and sound levels for ingredients and their placement.
[*] Fixes an issue causing the UI to disappear after fast-traveling.
[/list]

[h3]Other[/h3]
[list]
[*] Halloween content has been disabled by default. If you enjoyed it and want to retain that content in your game, please enable it in the options menu.
[*] Japanese language has been added to the game.
[*] Simplified Chinese has been improved.
[/list]

And that would be it for the update, folks. We hope that you’ll enjoy the changes and new features that we’ve added to the game.

notes.title: Update #1 is here + Halloween Content.
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/36e8def916a5206d4f58e598556f7f1a9b0a6302.jpg[/img]

Food Truck Simulator’s first larger update is here. It fixes and improved a lot of issues, adds new things and features some neat Halloween content. Enjoy!


[h3]Halloween[/h3]
[i]This update adds Halloween related content to the game. This content will not be removed after Halloween, so you can enjoy it whenever you feel like it.[/i] 
For that purpose you’ll have a button in the menu to enable or disable Halloween related content.
The following Halloween content has been added:
[list]
[*] Exterior decorations for the food truck.
[*] Interior decorations for the food truck.
[*] New decorations for the garage.
[*] New garage wall decoration.
[*] All selling points have been decorated.
[*] Decoration throughout the city added.
[*] A special Halloween song for the gas station job added.
[/list]

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
[list]
[*] Free roam is now available right away. You don’t need to finish the story mode any longer in order to enjoy some sandbox action. There are 7 levels of prestige, each unlocking the following features: tools, devices, truck and garage customizations, new areas on the the map and selling points.
[*] You can now enter the back of the food truck while in the garage to manage storage or prepare ingredients that do now involve using the kitchen appliances.
[*] New selling spot mechanic. The selling points are now open 24 hours a day and have special 
[*] ‘Rush Hours’ during which the amount of customers is increased.
[*] Preparation time before cooking and some control over customer traffic via an open/close sign you control in sandbox mode in addition to the rush hour mechanics.
[/list]

[h3]Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] Keybidings have been redone. They now contain a lot more configuration options and are separated into categories now. A lot of the issues with key binds and mini-games have been resolved as well.
[*] Manual Saves have been added. You can now invoke saving your game manually in addition to the game’s auto-save feature. There are however a few limitations for the time being as you can’t manually save in selling points, during sabotage or when in a dialog. We plan to have those restrictions removed in the next update.
[*] Assembling recipes has seen some improvement by expanding tray and boxes logic so you can easier and faster assemble the recipe having either item in hand and putting the ingredients inside.
[*] The Tray itself has also been improved. You can grab the tray and collect slices of food while holding the tray. You can now also add multiple slices. We did the same thing for the food boxes so you can hold them now and put things directly into them.

notes.title: Beefing up our gas stations - we want your ideas!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/6eba3165c06a1e3a0f646a22004250110cc8f945.jpg[/img]

The majority of the things you do in Food Truck Simulator relate to arranging the food truck's interior and exterior, planning purchases, driving the food truck and of course preparing the actual dishes. We've written about those things in the previous DevLogs and you could experience some of them for yourself in the demo or during the recent Playtest. Or you can do it for real next week on September 14th when the games becomes available to buy.

At the beginning of August the teams behind [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1149620/Gas_Station_Simulator/]Gas Station Simulator[/url] and Food Truck Simulator had a bit of an argument concerning having [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1149620/view/3363644258063773265]a food truck on a gas station[/url] in Gas Station Simulator. We've asked the player base for opinions and thoughts and we've received a ton of ideas on suggestions on how to improve on that idea. Chief among those was to keep the mechanics, but a food trailer would fit a lot better than a food truck. Anyway, the team did put that onto their to-do list as right now they are busy with a birthday surprise, because it's been a year since the game was released.

Either way, the folks working on Food Truck Simulator decided that maybe that’s an opportunity to grab something from Gas Station Simulator. As you might be aware, there are [b]several gas stations[/b] in Food Truck Simulator. You can fill up your food truck there, but you can also do some tasks for the people running those gas stations. Once completed, you will be able to fast travel to those gas stations, among other rewards.

Those gas station jobs are related to the usual tasks, often involving keeping that place in shape, cleaning etc. Something that is also at the core of Gas Station Simulator. And this is where it might get very interesting for the future: are there any mechanics you like in Gas Station Simulator that you’d like us to port to the gas stations in Food Truck Simulator?

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1149620/Gas_Station_Simulator/

The reason we are putting that question out there is simple: moving some mechanics that fits from another of our game is likely to be something we can do relatively quick and as we are slowly firming up the plans for post-launch content for Food Truck Simulator, now would be the perfect time for any of those ideas. So let us know in the discussion using the [b]Discuss[/b] button below.

notes.title: Managing Crucial Aspects
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35762680/450031e3a02457e7a002462ffe3069a41c284ed9.jpg[/img]

Whether your business is handling or running four wheels or running on four wheels, there are a few basic rules to follow. When you master these common factors, you will become really a business shark in an ocean of opportunities. Let's analyze two economic activities that may become yours even today: [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1160920/Food_Truck_Simulator/]Food Truck[/url] and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1149620/Gas_Station_Simulator/]Gas Station[/url]. 

[h3]Renown[/h3]
Fame has different appearances and in Gas Station Simulator we like to call it "popularity". If an adventure on Route 66 is still ahead of you, popularity is a system that tracks feedback from your customers. Do not exceed the required amount of fuel while fulfilling the order. Check out each product carefully and do not scatter them on the floor. Take care of the gas station so that it is clean and its shelves are not empty. These and many other activities contribute to increased popularity, which means higher traffic, the possibility of further expanding and developing the gas station and unique visual rewards. For those who are struggling to reach the maximum popularity level, we hear you! We are working on a new way to increase popularity to make leveling more enjoyable.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35762680/f21b9cefc2d1d79f4434bacc75a79d4280962c00.jpg[/img]

For [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1160920/Food_Truck_Simulator/]Food Truck Simulator[/url], based on the experience and feedback in Gas Station Simulator, we have created a new system called  “prestige” that approaches this topic slightly differently. There is nothing more sensitive than a customer with an empty belly, and as a chef and salesman you will meet many of them. Be careful because such a customer might be a ticking bomb that will damage your prestige when exploding. How to avoid it? Feed them properly. Keep an eye on the ingredients and don't make them wait too long. Take care of cleanliness! Nobody wants to eat a grilled burger that's wrapped in burnt fat. If you manage to do it, it will open up a whole host of new opportunities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35762680/1413f6765a67eb9326be89cdda6f483e01cfe561.jpg[/img]

[h3]Time[/h3]
If you thought you would have peace of mind at a gas station in the middle of nowhere, then you are almost right. The business beginnings are usually slow, and later on you can either take a break by closing the gas station or get help by hiring employees. Nevertheless, once you spread your wings and start offering fuel, a cool drink or a bathroom as the only place within dozens of miles, don't be surprised when a wave of customers floods you. May you be prepared for this in advance and have a warehouse full of products and tanks full of fuel. Time is not your ally, so keep an eye on it.
In Food Truck Simulator, time management begins in the garage. Plan a route, analyze all strategic places, and when you are ready, start the engine and show off with your driving skills. If you manage to get to the supply store on time before the competition, you will get a better offer. Be late and pay full price like any other. The next stop? The selling point where the time and mass of hungry customers stand against your kitchen under your command.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35762680/6cbdd52502c4de4ffafa88c2d538216e8390b97b.jpg[/img]
	
[h3]Progress[/h3]
	This point applies to both your business and you personally. Let's start with the Food Truck. Traveling through the corners of the city, makes you discover new locations that will provide a greater business range. You meet new people, thanks to whom you will expand your service scope. Over time, your vehicle will become a better mobile kitchen, and you will become a better driver which will allow you to get to further places faster. However, you can also focus on any single selling point. Focus on your favorite type of kitchen, which will please both you and the consumer. Some say that a good cook is not one who has trained 10,000 dishes, but one who practiced a dish  10,000 times. 
	And how to manage this in a desert? Las Vegas and Dubai were also built on empty sand. So remember the day you wake up for the first time as the owner of this not very spectacular abandoned gas station. Think of it a month later as you enter a huge and refurbished facility. Recall the initial silence when you hear the clamor of constant engines and people around you. When you go inside the workshop to save a customer's vacation or use the car wash to make sure someone's date goes well, think of the piles of sand that stood where these structures are now. The future is in your hands.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35762680/823299ccf1a1bce6258c454be19772c285b70db1.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35762680/4b3917b75a739cc1f55879351e151dd700d45d1b.jpg[/img]

[h3]Express yourself[/h3]
	This is your business. You are your own boss and don't be afraid to show it in an artistic way. Whether it's a gas station or a food truck, you'll start your working day with a smile when you look at your handiwork with pride. There are plenty of customisation options in both games and we intend to add even more!

notes.title: DevLog #12: Cruisin' around the street
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/6a81a168927e55fadf74a37686272f013868f8c5.jpg[/img]

Driving your truck around town in Food Truck Simulator is a staple element of our gameplay loop. 

We wanted to, in some small way, accurately present the feel and difficulty of driving around town.
Before you set off on the crowded streets, don't forget to visually prepare your vehicle, which we touched upon with the previous devlog.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/dbad5af510bc5e92079e435b4c7cc5e8442c4dd1.jpg[/img]

A good vibe, music playing on the radio, and we're ready to set off.

Traveling around the map via your truck will allow you to collect various collectibles, unlocking such things as new paints, layouts, car wheel trimmings, mirrors, bumpers or unique decorations for the top of the truck. You will have to keep your eyes open and try a little when searching for them, though.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/154e8673d2327e05f88592200ed3cbd45dc4bcb6.jpg[/img]

An equally important element is picking up orders we will have to deliver to Clara's shop. Every order delivered under a certain time from a specific location will grant us bonuses in the form of discounts, so swift and agile maneuvering through the crowded streets will have a tangible impact on our wallet.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/1a49a955787826daa1565dc1a5c2dcc15671c0bc.jpg[/img]

Driving also requires fuel, and the logic is preserved in our game. We don't have an infinite fuel supply (seeing as the prices are terribly high nowadays), so at first, we're limited to what we have in our garage tank. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/316835b3e34599f1f6cb3478203beca1a4c6b597.jpg[/img]

During normal gameplay, you will be able to refuel at gas stations all around the city.

For those who aren't as fond of driving, we've prepared a fast-travel system for the late game. You will be able to use it to move around between various different gas stations.

notes.title: DevLog#11: Show your style
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/cd8afba4df6fcc7b4b21e9ea7cd2e8614a6fc637.jpg[/img]

If you've ever watched Ty Pennington turn houses into works of art on "Extreme Makeover" with bated breath, you'll love this part of our gameplay.

As you know, Food Truck Simulator lets you use a Customization tab to retrofit your food truck according to your wishes.
At first, you'll begin by picking one of the three paint jobs available from the start to paint your restaurant-on-wheels. These will serve as the basis for your future decorative deeds.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/4d3c1cf0e285ba6b836c0ab42c6a172754ef9b05.gif[/img]

Next, we're moving to the layouts, which will give your truck that characteristic look and show a little bit of yourself in the design as well. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/d9d5c098c18790b76d730fc06bbe617dde19cefa.gif[/img]

Just like with the paint jobs, the number of initial layouts is limited, but that does not mean that it is the extent of your artistic expression. Layouts, just like paints and wheel jobs and other decorative elements, can be found as collectibles strewn around the map. Gathering them will expand your repertoire of customizing your vehicle to your precise needs.

You will also be able to change the mirrors, darken glass or add an additional roof element which will make your food truck stand out that much more.

But that's not all, because as we've mentioned at the beginning, you will also be able to customize your garage's interior. We know that there's nothing cozier than a cozy home. You will be able to change your office from the inside and the outside, your bedroom, your mezzanine, and the entirety of the interior in general.

notes.title: DevLog#10: Meet your neighbors!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/fc83eaa37843d3c31a8068b82817c5029d5f1e7b.jpg[/img]

[b]Our lovely Clara![/b]

She's the person without who you'd likely not even start the business. An invaluable source of insight on every level.

It's thanks to her that you'll learn the secrets of running your enterprise-on-wheels. From arranging your kitchen, perfectly ordering new products, learning how to fire off your grill, to preparing delicious dishes and remembering that it's high time to rest sometimes.

She's almost like a mom, making sure you're taken care of and that nothing bad happens to you, ever.
You can always count on her, even in the most dire of circumstances. And if you're quick on picking up your delivery, she might just give you a discount.

Nurture this relationship, because Clara will always come in handy!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/e347cc4391de3533521dcc64c43edc41c4a35d5a.jpg[/img]

[b]This guy really doesn't need any additional introductions.[/b]

He's the ideal example of someone who did NOT age like fine wine. It's easy to say that almost everyone met a guy like Dennis sometime in their lives and no doubt won't forget the whole ordeal.

Dennis did some growing up since you've last met him in Gas Station Simulator, but he did not change one bit.

Now, he'll be your main rival in conquering the city's fast-food empire.
Will you be able to get back at him after all these years? No doubt most of you dream precisely of that chance!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/96fb9fb842fee0296c083b87c264d60aef3d9c5d.jpg[/img]

[b]There is only one king of the Italian district.[/b]

This son of Sicilian immigrants gives the citizens of Westside Port a taste of his homeland cuisine and never fails to impress.

Likewise, he won't fail to impress you. He's the first one (right after Clara, that is) to extend a helping hand when you'll it most.

Remember him when though times come to your food truck enterprise.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/83640eb51161d9b85e1045b4cb5009df17135289.jpg[/img]

[b]This guy is busy with his job 24/7. [/b]

He loves it... and the 'it' is being in a gas station all day.

Yes, yes, you've read that right. Food Truck Simulator also has its own gas stations. Aside from allowing you to refuel, Joe will also help you earn a few bucks on the side.

The man appreciates every pair of extra hands, so make sure to map the spots where you'll be able to find him.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/a3aa7c3fd39bbd99167c1f9e70a6de7da6056ebf.jpg[/img]

[b]The mystery man from the Asian district.[/b]

He knew your father very well, but was content to keeping in the shadows. Supposedly he has access to wondrous ingredients, yet the question remains whether he'll fancy sharing them with you.

That relationship might be very interesting. Maybe it'll play out like in Karate Kid?
You - Daniel-san. Him - Mr. Miyagi. And a whole bunch of planks to shatter?

How do you feel about that?
Soon you'll be able to see for yourself!

Thanks to all the feedback we received about the demo we decided to update it before the game’s release. We payed a lot of attention to the performance some of you mentioned and made massive improvements here. And a lot more:

[h3]Driving[/h3]
We improved the driving experience with the food truck and put some more work into the handling of the vehicle.

[h3]Cooking[/h3]
Lots of smaller tweaks and a reworked cutting mechanics should make it more enjoyable.

We added some more upgrades to the food truck and also changed some of the customisations accessible via the customization/upgrade tabs in the UI.

notes.title: DevLog #9: Place for a Bite - Part 2
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/c6eac1699090991833e886851b97ceaccddfb09d.jpg[/img]

Welcome back to the second part of DevLog about game locations.

We hope you liked the previous locations and are ready for more.
So now you can sit back, relax and check out the rest of our delicious spots.

[h3][b]MARINA  [/b][/h3]
A breath of fresh air and... grilled fish.

I'm sure you know this first hand. Each time you show up in any seaside place, that smell will stay with you for the rest of your stay.

Happily, it doesn't work like that here.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/51ac99f66d92b66c1e6369608e3fb515ef41d176.gif[/img]

At the Marina Selling Point, you'll be able to serve pizza and fish, but luckily only as sushi.

The cool sea breeze will help you work over the burning-hot pizza oven. The clients are pretty chill too. Thankfully not asking if the order's ready every 2 minutes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/42fef602daa862d37a25336216d711c9a86c74fe.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]SHIPYARD[/b][/h3]
Working at a shipyard's no easy feat. It's hard work and buckets of sweat that translate into a mean hunger, so... there's no better place for you and your truck than right here.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/a5c530972e425aa647c927a8eab525fb4a266c67.gif[/img]

It's here that you'll serve a mountain-load of fries along with some delicious Italian pizza.
You'll learn more and more recipes, so be careful and precise when assembling your orders.
Will that mean better tips for your efforts? Don't overthink it, pull your sleeves up and get to work.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/812dc7e36126e3cd16b03ea71c9097a6c4853d41.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]ASIAN DISTRICT[/b][/h3]
Can you break through in the Asian District like Bruce Lee in "Enter the Dragon"?

This spot is an ideal location to see whether you are a real sushi master. See how well you can put together those futomaki rolls.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/675e27a2efddfc217c808dd646660a6cd2b125af.gif[/img]

[b]Sushi History Fact [/b]- The inventor of modern sushi is believed to be Hanaya Yohei, who invented nigiri-zushi, a type of sushi most known today, in which seafood is placed on hand-pressed vinegared rice, around 1824 in the Edo period (1603–1867). It was the fast food of the chōnin class in the Edo period.

In addition, the Asian District also allows you to serve the good ol' Belgian treat - fries.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/b19f5b5263990d6c9e4ce8a6d4fdc153ba41680b.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]BEACH[/b][/h3]
The perfect place for spending leisure time.

It's here that you'll be able to charm hungry surfers, tourists, friends and italian town amateurs with you delightful recipes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/12554a54916ea207232c459df496cb4628cc02c3.gif[/img]

Make sure to bring enough pizza dough, sushi rice and all the other ingredients though!
In places such as these the eating ends just moments before the sundown.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/8b35feea2cc1f0fd7f91cb6e1c95054bf428a6be.jpg[/img]

[b]So, ready to conquer the city?

Get in your restaurant-on-wheels and show them what'chu got!

notes.title: DevLog #8: Place for a Bite - Part 1
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/ce485275a07ee0b5da2e07aeb1ec1f0e0fa3fe16.jpg[/img]

As we all know, hungry people can be found anywhere. 
We just never know how hungry they might be, or what they might fancy at that particular time. 

Our in-game locations function in a similar manner, but thankfully you'll have a chance to prepare. Eventually you'll master figuring out where to find people looking for the juiciest burger, a proper Italian pizza, a delicious Belgian potato treat or Japanese rolled rice.

[h3][b]SERENITY PARK[/b][/h3]
You'll begin your adventure in Serenity Park. It's here that you'll take your first steps on your culinary journey, following in the path of your father, serving real beef treats. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/bcb98eb49ec46ad4565ca8b9fd9f9f38ef08f4ed.gif[/img]

Always remember what your clients demand! Time, doneness and order precision are key. 
The calm atmosphere of the appropriately-named Serenity Park will ease you into your new grand adventure.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/b26c600a19f8ed000a31f744d382e793625e9f31.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]NIGHT CLUBS [/b][/h3]
It's said that those who do not try cooking for a whole bunch of others do not know what true work really means. Doubly so if it's in the middle of the night. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/d0d981a85629e25aba8b8dc4e53e878b4db2536a.gif[/img]

The next selling point on your journey - the Night Clubs - will teach you how to prepare true potato delicacies - fries. 

[b]Fries History Fact time[/b] - fries were apparently invented in the XVIII century in a Belgian town named Dinant during a cold winter. The rivers of the nearby river were frozen over, and without fish people instead began peeling potatoes into small boat-shapes while frying them to try and replace the fish. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/800cebf141d8a4ccb662e3352ba90143220fcbe4.jpg[/img]

Thankfully, fries are no longer fish replacements and have evolved into something that truly pleases the taste buds. Just like with the burger, time, doneness and ingredients are all key.

[h3][b]BUSINESS PARK[/b][/h3]
There's no relaxing in the Business Park, and thus "time is money" takes on a whole different meaning.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/1486cd22c41aa5be220e3ddf7dfa814d3acf1e4b.gif[/img]

Regularly schedule lunch breaks guarantee a rush hour of hungry clients and their work stress hardly makes things better. 

The different tastes here are far, far wilder than before, and thus it is here you will learn the secrets of sushi-making.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/8504b90811e95457c7b66ae5c2271edbfc8e4e29.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]ITALIAN DISTRICT [/b][/h3]     
Buongiorno a tutti!

Welcome to our beautiful, little piece of Italy. 
Here, live follows its own rhythm. Here, you can slow down and catch your breath - but don't stop too long. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/a08e509ac6831c29344c204dc3ac248919ccf3bf.gif[/img]

Flour, yeast, water, salt and olive oil - those are the basics of a successful dough. After that, it's all up to you. 

Let your Italian spirit take hold of you, and show your clients what you're really made of. Aside from pizza, the Italian District will also gladly share in your expertise of expertly-cooked burgers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/d31ac2d7a06c905aeaa2daa0c6af3fda02e30656.jpg[/img]

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/14fe51513fce6a286f790bcd7ff4bcda46a17810.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/282c0959a1b0438d5be860d3f3b8cdd9abe90e20.gif[/img]

A hungry client is, obviously, an angry client. A hungry client who got the wrong order... well, you can guess for yourselves.

Each order consists of multiple steps. Such as preparing the actual meal, assembling the order and finally handing it out.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/147cbfd643cd60f4d66546a71c257e7a5d9a7f09.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/fcb7b022bab7cdb4ededa1f92b1e7f78b93960b5.gif[/img]

The folks working on Gas Station Simulator aren’t resting either. Just today we announced the first DLC for the game: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1940030/Gas_Station_Simulator__Can_Touch_This_DLC/?beta=0

Called “Can Touch This”, the DLC deals with a wide range of new and exciting customization options for the gas station, workshop and warehouse.

Customizing walls and roofs, changing the placement of windows, doors, trashcans or cash register are rounded up with decals you can spray anywhere on your gas station, more interior & exterior decorations and also more levels and employees! And all that already in May at just $2.99 :)

The reason we write about the DLC here is not only to let you know, but what we did for this DLC will actually become very relevant to Food Truck Simulator. We will actually grab some of the things the team developed for the DLC and use them in Food Truck Simulator to open up a bit more customization options than we initially intended and that without having to spend a lot of time on it :)

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/dbd64901e8860b468a776ea1b5ad185472cc3fab.jpg[/img]

Hello Food Truckers,

It's been a rough few days for us, but we are extremely grateful for all the feedback and bugs you've sent our way. We are always trying to push the quality forward and we can't stress enough how important your feedback is to us.

Today, we are releasing a bigger update for Food Truck Simulator, addressing performance, controls, saving, and additional bug fixes that proved to be a major issues for the players.

Below you can find specific details of what has been addressed in this update:

[list]
[*] Fixed saving system
[*] Improvement of visuals
[*] Slight improvement of performance
[*] Added "inverted mouse" option
[*] Added "sensitivity" option for mouse
[*] Improvement of traffic behaviour
[*] Localisation fixes
[*] Most common bugs fixes
[*] Fixed collectables saving
[*] Fixed bug affecting credits
[*] Truck fuelling improvement
[*] Collision improvement
[*] Added context to certain NPCs
[*] Improvement of cutting mechanics
[*] Improvement of cooking mechanics
[*] Fixed bug affecting map
[*] Added valve animation to refuelling
[*] Improved quality of some materials
[/list]

We are planning to further address issues within the game and improve it's quality as we are already working on another fixes.

Please, feel free to send us any issues connected with the game on our Discord or in the Discussions on Steam.

notes.title: DevLog #4: Driving the Food Truck
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/93abec4527982d676e4f95d47ecf1323ecaba2de.jpg[/img]

Ever since we announced Food Truck Simulator we continuously received feedback about making the food truck drivable. Especially lately this seems to be the top request. 

Now, initially we didn’t plan on driving the food truck as such, but similar to the player feedback, the notion to drive it kept coming back every now and then during development meetings and testing sessions. 

So it was just a matter of time before we caved in and now we made the decision to pursue the food truck become freely drivable. We are currently prototyping the driving itself, but the bigger challenge than driving the food truck are the other cars on the streets and traffic in general. 
While parking the food truck on the map allowed us to use traffic that just looked nice, driving the food truck yourself requires the traffic to by fully dynamic and react to all your actions.

Our other game, Gas Station Simulator, has a basic dynamic traffic system that we ported to Food Truck Simulator and really ramped it up over the past months. As a result, we now have a fully featured traffic system in place with rush hours, roadworks, jams, accidents and everything else that you’d expect from traffic in a city.

With that major obstacle sorted, we are now working on the driving behavior of the food truck itself, which as mentioned is the way smaller task. 
Please note that the screenshot above shows an incomplete food truck interior, it's just a placeholder for the time being, but we really wanted to show you something from the driving. You can expect us to show you some in-game footage in the upcoming weeks as we decided to make it part of the game’s demo we started working on.

notes.title: DevLog #4: "The Route Matters"
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/5e247e70a292bc4804c9670e16241fdd3107d76d.jpg[/img]

It’s morning, your truck is full of gas but only so-so full of produce. You’ve got most of the day booked, dedicated to serving food for the hungry pedestrians and moving back and forth lucrative positions we’ve spoken about at length before. Sounds like a lot? Because it is. But that’s not the whole picture, oh no. We’ve touched upon picking the right location, managing your stock and food, but all of these were essentially the snapshots of the ‘key’ bits. Now let’s talk about the glue between each of these frames - Travel.

Each morning you’ll find yourself greeted with a few key pieces of information. The daily event schedule, news and weather forecast. As you can imagine, each and every piece of aforementioned information will affect moving about the city. Events such as rock concerts or scheduled roadworks will cause traffic jams and congestions. News will keep you up to date on all the seemingly unexpected happenings (such as, for example, runaway tigers from the local circus) and finally, the weather will affect how you drive directly.

Don’t worry, you don’t need to have a license to drive (in this game, at least!). We’ll be driving for you. That is to say, your food truck will. All you need to do is select the destination, all the waypoints towards it and adjust the speed at which you’re actually moving. As you can imagine, traffic jams and closed streets will cost you time - and time is both the freshness of your ingredients and the priority of those lucrative locations we’ve told you about. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/01e457b1221bbad368f61ec8f85965410569ef72.jpg[/img]

Speed plays a factor too, and is very much a double-edged sword. Move fast and get places fast. Move faster and risk getting the police all suss’ about your sudden speeding. Or worse, an immediate crash into the nearby lamp post and prompt visit to the mechanic. And that’s a day ruined.

The route’s important for one more reason. Don’t expect the morning produce to serve you for the entire day (or stay fresh, for that matter). Every so often, you will have to order extras, and stop by the vendors to pick up your, well, orders. This will usually take you away from the direct route from the next golden spot, but what use is a beach full of hungry people when you don’t have food in the fridge to even begin serving? It’s all about your tactics here.

Don’t worry. You’ll be able to review all the important information before you rev the engine each time. So make sure to plan ahead and plan dynamically.

notes.title: DevLog #3 “Menu Matters”
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/c1c86813fec7d0caaa3a87e5b2383fcc641b3121.png[/img]
The menu plays a special role in Food Truck Simulator. It is not just a visual asset to make your food truck look more food truck-ish, it serves an actual purpose and a really important one.
As a matter of fact, in a way the menu is one of the most important aspects of running your food truck. The menu is something you define each day before you leave your base. You can only sell items that are on the menu. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/aff050e2ec4db7003cb135479cd3edce1432b6d2.png[/img]
What goes onto the menu is dictated by the location that you want to set up at and obviously the storage capacity of your food truck. In the early stages of the game, refrigerated storage will be your limiting factor, later on this shouldn’t be an issue. Another major factor is what dishes you are comfortable preparing. 
While it’s wise to prepare the menu before setting off, the menu by all means is not static. You can change it anytime, and sometimes you will need to. When you run out of certain ingredients and are unable to make some of the dishes or run out of goods like soda or coffee, leaving them on the menu while not being able to sell them will result in unsatisfied customers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/b7a083e7dbeb13e446bb59d75d6d1e9170015f3c.png[/img]
Running out of things is obviously not the only reason to alter the menu. Another one is when changing locations, not to mention if it gets late. While you might offer tea, coffee and soda during the day, should you stay out longer, at least adding beer or wine to the menu in the evening won’t hurt your income.

The further you progress into the game and the better you equip your food truck, the more items the menu will be able to hold. While you start out with only 5 positions on the menu, you’ll quickly upgrade it to 7, 10 and then later on all the way up to 25 items that can put on the menu.

notes.title: DevLog #2 “Location Matters”
notes.content:
You've got a fridge full of ingredients and enough fuel to visit all the important venues. 
Enough to turn a good profit of course, but maybe there's a way to get even more buck for your bang. Owning a food truck is more than just having quick hands and being good with a knife and the deep fryer. To truly become the best of the best, you will need to show you can use *tactics*. People are picky eaters, and not everyone will approach the fat, cheese-dripping hamburger with the same hungry gaze in their eye. Stocking up on food means stocking up the right types of meals for the right venues, and those we have aplenty. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/f959505e56d22adb33d07eeb1d3aefdc3e3e2cc2.png[/img]

Take the business district, for example. Over here, people spend their entire days in picturesque, but sweltering-hot glass towers, inside cubicles and offices where the AC works without failure only so very often. Naturally, your customers will find themselves ordering drinks to every meal they may think of, and even these will fall into specific categories. Light foods that do not require too much energy to digest, low on fat, yet rich in carbohydrates. Salads, greens, vegetarian and vegan fillings to make the burger as succulent as always, but half as heavy in calories. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35860079/4bc8c16f9c8af4f90f04d211abad35feb1a7df82.jpg[/img]

On the opposite end of town, the skyscrapers are yet to raise. Instead, men and women work and sweat on construction yards in impressive, yet bare frameworks of the office buildings yet to come. These people are hardy, tired and usually very hungry, so gin and salad will not only fail to satisfy, but easily break a dozen safety regulations straight from the get go. To cater well, you will have to prepare foods rich in power and protein to satisfy the rigorous needs of a blue collar worker. 

Sounds like a lot? Nobody said owning a food truck will be easy! But with enough skill and some trial and error, it won't take you long to get a good feel of your clientele. And when you satisfy the customers' needs for sweet, sweet food you will get to bask in the sweet, sweet profit. Good luck!

notes.title: DevLog #1 “Vehicle Maintenance”
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=MCZgdJTdaOk;full][/previewyoutube]

Buying an old food truck, restoring it to working condition and equipping it with everything you need for a mobile kitchen are an important part of the game. Having done that however does not mean you are done with your vehicle. Whenever you travel from location to location, prepare the dishes and serve your customers, your food truck is being used. As with all things being used, they require some maintenance. 

You obviously have to clean the kitchen equipment every now and then or more frequently when things go wrong and you make a mess. But your food truck itself needs proper vehicle maintenance, too. Tires and brakes won’t last forever, oil has to be checked and topped up or the filter needs a change. Yes, you have to fill the tank regularly as well, your food truck doesn’t run on hot air, you know.

Those are the things you have to take care for on more or less regular basis. Then there are things that just happen and will need fixing. A broken mirror here, a demolished windshield wiper here or a smashed light because you just had to make fun of your competition and some light vandalism was their reply. 

Taking care of your food truck’s mechanical state is not just a nice gimmick. It also comes with its own events like a policeman writing you a ticket for a broken headlight. Not being able to get on time to a profitable locations for the lunch break because you broke down will cut into your earnings even more than a ticket. We are implementing a series of such events associated with the vehicle itself to make it more interesting and provide some real consequences to neglecting your food truck.

Vehicle maintenance is not something you will do all the time. The primary goal in Food Truck Simulator is still to serve your customers. Taking care of your vehicle and simulating usage over time just adds another layer of realism to the game we felt would enhance the immersion of running a food truck in all its aspects.
